mcqs.q: The STOP-R index estimates rabies elimination capacity using which type of data?
o: Country-level infrastructure indicators (literacy, infant mortality, electricity access, political stability, natural hazards)
Genetic sequences of rabies virus variants
mcqs.e: The index was built from five publicly available country-level infrastructure indicators, not direct surveillance.

mcqs.q: Projected global human rabies deaths in DMRVV-endemic countries from 2022 to 2030 are expected to:
mcqs.e: Estimates fall from ~40,111 in 2022 to ~32,349 in 2030.

mcqs.q: A key interpretation of the study was that rabies elimination success is:
o: Influenced by factors external to rabies programs such as country infrastructure
mcqs.e: The authors concluded external infrastructural factors influence elimination progress.

mcqs.q: Dog bite incidence was highest among which group?
mcqs.e: Dog bite incidence peaked in children under 10 and in males.

mcqs.q: Bacteria were isolated most frequently from:
mcqs.e: Cat bites yielded bacteria in 21.5% versus only 3% of dog bites.

mcqs.q: Cat bite incidence was highest among:
mcqs.e: Cat bite incidence was highest in adults aged ≥80 and in females.

mcqs.q: Which factor was identified as a frequent warning signal for biting incidents?
o: Owner's suspected substance or animal abuse and antisocial behaviour
mcqs.e: Owner substance/animal abuse and antisocial behaviour were among the most prevalent warning factors.

mcqs.q: The authors concluded that a proportion of owners of confiscated dogs:
o: Always comply with muzzle and leash obligations
May not be willing or capable of guaranteeing societal safety
mcqs.e: Owner aggression and poor adherence to prior obligations suggested some cannot guarantee public safety.

mcqs.q: Reports mentioning ≥5 ownership factors were:
o: Equally common in both time frames
Twice as frequent in 2020–22 as in 2008–10
Less common in the recent period
mcqs.e: Such reports were 38% in tf2 versus 16% in tf1.

mcqs.q: Rocky Mountain spotted fever is caused by:
mcqs.e: RMSF is a tick-borne disease caused by Rickettsia rickettsii.

mcqs.q: RMSF case fatality in Mexico compared with the US is:
mcqs.e: US fatality is 5–7% while Mexican case fatality often exceeds 30%.

mcqs.q: The recommended urgent treatment for symptomatic RMSF is:
mcqs.e: Prompt doxycycline is emphasized for symptomatic patients.

mcqs.q: The kennel outbreak of Brucella canis was most likely caused by:
o: Introduction of one infected imported dog
mcqs.e: WGS showed all isolates in one cluster, consistent with a single introduced index dog.

mcqs.q: Among contact dogs, the seroprevalence of B. canis antibodies was approximately:
mcqs.e: 23 of 69 contact dogs (34%) were seropositive by SAT.

mcqs.q: Whole-genome sequencing of the outbreak isolates showed they:
mcqs.e: All isolates belonged to the same cluster, supporting a single source.

mcqs.q: Human exposure to Brucella canis in this case occurred when:
o: An infected dog aborted in the aircraft cabin
mcqs.e: An infected dog aborted in the passenger cabin, exposing passengers and crew.

mcqs.q: The report recommends Brucella screening of:
o: Sexually intact dogs prior to breeding, purchase, or transport
mcqs.e: Screening sexually intact dogs before breeding, purchase, or transport is emphasized.

mcqs.q: The transport of pregnant dogs was characterized as:
o: A previously unrecognized public health threat
mcqs.e: It was flagged as a previously unrecognized public health threat plus a welfare concern.

mcqs.q: All canine nontyphoidal Salmonella strains in the study carried:
o: AMR determinants for critically/highly important drug classes
mcqs.e: Every strain had AMR determinants for WHO critically/highly important antibiotics.

mcqs.q: The study concluded that companion animals should be:
o: Included in One Health antimicrobial-resistance biosurveillance
mcqs.e: Authors stressed One Health biosurveillance encompassing companion animals.

mcqs.q: Genomic comparison found human NTS isolates that were:
mcqs.e: Sixteen human isolates were closely related to dog-associated strains, supporting zoonotic potential.

mcqs.q: HPAI H5 virus infection was reported in how many wild bird species?
mcqs.e: Infection was reported across 51 bird species.

mcqs.q: The species groups with the highest reported mortality:
o: Varied per epidemic year (geese versus sea birds)
mcqs.e: 2020–21 hit Anatidae/barnacle geese; 2021–22 hit sea birds like Sandwich terns and gannets.

mcqs.q: The recommended surveillance approach was to:
o: Monitor live and dead wild birds
mcqs.e: Monitoring live and dead wild birds was recommended for tracking HPAI dynamics.

mcqs.q: The Salmonella Vitkin outbreak was linked to:
mcqs.e: Cases were tied to pet bearded dragons, including an isolate from an enclosure.

mcqs.q: Most affected US patients were:
mcqs.e: Two-thirds of US patients were under 1 year old.

mcqs.q: Traceback of the bearded dragons identified a potential common supplier in:
mcqs.e: At least one common supplier in Southeast Asia was identified.

mcqs.q: The most plausible source of H5N1 infection in mammals was:
o: Close contact with or ingestion of infected birds
mcqs.e: Close contact with and ingestion of infected birds was the most plausible source.

mcqs.q: Compared with previous waves, the current panzootic affected:
o: A larger geographic area and more mammal species
Fewer species and a smaller area
mcqs.e: >48 species across 26 countries, a far larger scope than prior waves.

mcqs.q: The review warns that H5N1 may be:
o: Adapting to infect mammals, raising pandemic concern
mcqs.e: Mutations and possible mammal-to-mammal transmission suggest adaptation and pandemic risk.

mcqs.q: The emerging parasite reported in US dogs and cats is:
mcqs.e: The cases involved the eyeworm Thelazia callipaeda.

mcqs.q: Phylogenetic analysis suggested the parasite was introduced from:
mcqs.e: Phylogenetics indicated a European origin.

mcqs.q: The authors recommend which approach to limit further spread?
mcqs.e: A One Health approach was advised to limit spread in North America.

mcqs.q: Canine Borrelia burgdorferi seroprevalence in NW North Carolina changed from 2017 to 2021 by:
mcqs.e: Seroprevalence rose from 2.2% in 2017 to 11.2% in 2021.

mcqs.q: The spatial pattern of canine seroprevalence shifted from:
mcqs.e: Moran's I shifted from clustered (0.30) in 2017 to dispersed (−0.20) in 2021.

mcqs.q: The study supports using canine seroprevalence data primarily to:
o: Monitor human risk for Lyme disease
mcqs.e: Individual-level canine data were endorsed as a sentinel for human Lyme disease risk.
